Treatment summary
The patient presented following a low-speed head-on collision with a knee injury that is consistent with the kind and force of the
impact described. Over the course of nine visits, care included evaluation, conservative management, and progressive
reassessment. The course of treatment ran somewhat lonegr than is typical for this type of injury, which we attribute to the
patient's gradual rate of functional recovery. On examination, several findings support the presence of a true knee injury,
including localized tenderness and reduced range of motion on the affected side. Other tests performed during the evaluation
returned normal results. The patient's history includes a minor strain in the same region several years ago, which resolved fully
without lasting limitation and does not appear to account for the current presentation. Billing records reflect single charges for
each service rendered, with no repeated or duplicate entries. Recovery is ongoing, and follow-up will continue to monitor
progress and adjust the plan of care as needed.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
